hypotheses.binder: (hEL : (EdgeSubset.mk (liftSubsetClosed (V.dropSubset (cutL n) (cutR n) s) (decide (V.boundaryFlag (cutL n) ∈ s))) hcL : EdgeSubset V).Eulerian)
hypotheses.justification: By `RS.Fragment.liftSubsetClosed_dropSubset` (GlueSubsetBij.lean:382), whose inputs are `hij : i ≠ j`, `hclosed` and closure of `s`, we get `liftSubsetClosed (V.dropSubset (cutL n) (cutR n) s) (decide (V.boundaryFlag (cutL n) ∈ s)) = s`. Here we supply `cutL_ne_cutR n` (already used in the proof), `hcl` and `hc`. Because the left side mentions `s`, `subst` cannot be used. Instead prove `∀ t (ht : t = s) hct, (EdgeSubset.mk t hct).Eulerian` by `rintro t rfl hct; exact hE`. This works because by proof irrelevance `EdgeSubset.mk s hct` and `EdgeSubset.mk s hc` are definitionally equal. Applying it to the lifted set, the lemma's equality and `hcL` recovers `hEL`, which is then passed to `isOut_unglue_glueDataClosed` as before. Nothing else in the statement mentions `hEL`. It can be deleted together with hneL.

hypotheses.binder: (hneL : Nonempty (EdgeSubset.mk (liftSubsetClosed (V.dropSubset (cutL n) (cutR n) s) (decide (V.boundaryFlag (cutL n) ∈ s))) hcL : EdgeSubset V).CanonData)
hypotheses.justification: Same argument as for hEL. `liftSubsetClosed_dropSubset (cutL_ne_cutR n) hcl s hc` shows the lifted set equals `s`. Then `∀ t (ht : t = s) hct, Nonempty (EdgeSubset.mk t hct).CanonData`, proved by `rintro t rfl hct; exact hne` (proof irrelevance makes the two EdgeSubsets definitionally equal), recovers `hneL` from `hne`. The rest of the proof is unchanged, and `hneL` is not mentioned elsewhere in the statement. It can be deleted together with hEL.
